samples.summary: New Slides "Remove link" button is wired to a caret-only `removeLink()`, so it silently no-ops when the user selects the linked text (the natural gesture) and the caret/focus lands outside the link run
samples.evidence: `TextBoxEditorAPI.removeLink` reads only `cursor.position` and bails when `findLinkRunAt(block, cursor.position.offset)` is undefined (packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:1234-1248); the selection range is never consulted. The new toolbar handler calls it unconditionally (packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/text-format-group.tsx:173-178, `removeLink()` is a no-op off a link, so an over-eager click costs nothing). In a text box whose content is e.g. "see example now" with the link on "example", Cmd+A / drag-select and click Remove link leaves the caret at the end of "now" → findLinkRunAt returns undefined → nothing happens, with no feedback. Since `onLinkRequest` is unwired in slides (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/slides-view.tsx:736-750) this button is the *only* link-removal path there, and Clear formatting no longer removes links, so the user is left with no working way to unlink unless they happen to park the caret inside the run. The fix belongs on `removeLink` (prefer the selection range / all link runs it covers when a selection exists) or on the new handler.

samples.summary: The new shared helper's documented invariant ("every caller that stores a caret-derived style has to ask this") is violated by the other caret-derived pending-style writers, which still re-arm `href` at a link trailing edge
samples.evidence: caret-style.ts's new doc block asserts that every caller storing a caret-derived style must consult `isAtLinkTrailingEdge` "or typing silently extends the link". Three out-of-diff callers do not: `applyStyleImpl`'s collapsed branch `pending.set({ ...getSelectionStyleImpl(), ...style }, cursor.position)` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1170 — reached by every toolbar toggle and by `stepSelectionFontSize` at :1283), and the text-box equivalent `pending.set({ ...base, fontSize: next }, ...)` (packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:884). At a link trailing edge the caret style carries the run's `href`, so e.g. toolbar-Bold then typing 'x' extends the hyperlink, while the same caret + Clear formatting now does not. Only Space/Enter/paste re-arm the exit (text-editor.ts:981, 4171), so plain typing does not self-heal. Existing behaviour, but the change makes the two paths disagree and states an invariant these sites do not honour.

samples.summary: The docs/slides text-box `clearInlineFormatting` is documented as matching the docs contract but is a silent no-op at a collapsed caret and never applies the new trailing-edge override
samples.evidence: The diff's updated JSDoc (packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:263-271) claims parity with `EditorAPI.clearInlineFormatting`, and slides delegates straight through (packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts:623-625). But `applyStyleImpl` here early-returns when there is no selection (packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:820), so with just a caret the slides Clear-formatting button does nothing (no pending style, unlike the docs editor), and the new `{ ...CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE, href: undefined }` trailing-edge override present in both other entry points is absent. The new text-box test only exercises the select-all/range path, so the divergence is unpinned.

samples.summary: Visual-harness baselines and the harness scenario description for the slides text-edit toolbar were not updated for the newly rendered Remove-link button
samples.evidence: The `slides-toolbar-text-editing` scenario renders the real `TextEditSection`, which now emits an extra Remove-link ToolbarButton; its description still reads "Shows FontSizePicker + TextFormatGroup (no strikethrough, no highlight) + TextParagraphGroup" (packages/frontend/src/app/harness/visual/slides-scenarios.tsx:1015), and the four committed baselines (packages/frontend/tests/visual/baselines/harness-visual.browser.slides-toolbar-text-editing{,.mobile,.desktop.dark,.mobile.dark}.png) are unchanged by this diff. The description staleness is not caught by any lane; the baseline drift will surface in the visual lane.

finding.summary: New Slides "Remove link" button is wired to a caret-only `removeLink()`, so it silently no-ops when the user selects the linked text (the natural gesture) and the caret/focus lands outside the link run
finding.evidence: `TextBoxEditorAPI.removeLink` reads only `cursor.position` and bails when `findLinkRunAt(block, cursor.position.offset)` is undefined (packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:1234-1248); the selection range is never consulted. The new toolbar handler calls it unconditionally (packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/text-format-group.tsx:173-178, `removeLink()` is a no-op off a link, so an over-eager click costs nothing). In a text box whose content is e.g. "see example now" with the link on "example", Cmd+A / drag-select and click Remove link leaves the caret at the end of "now" → findLinkRunAt returns undefined → nothing happens, with no feedback. Since `onLinkRequest` is unwired in slides (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/slides-view.tsx:736-750) this button is the *only* link-removal path there, and Clear formatting no longer removes links, so the user is left with no working way to unlink unless they happen to park the caret inside the run. The fix belongs on `removeLink` (prefer the selection range / all link runs it covers when a selection exists) or on the new handler.

verdict.reason: All claimed evidence verified. `TextBoxEditorAPI.removeLink` (packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:1234-1248) reads only `cursor.position` and returns silently when `findLinkRunAt(block, cursor.position.offset)` is undefined; it never consults `selection.range` (contrast `insertLink` at :1187-1188, which does branch on the selection). `findLinkRunAt` (packages/docs/src/view/link-run.ts:33-58) matches only an href-bearing inline containing/abutting the offset, and `TextEditor.selectAll()` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:3395-3412) parks the caret at the end of the last block — so Cmd+A over "see example now" with the link on "example" leaves the caret in a non-href run and the command no-ops. The new toolbar handler calls it unconditionally with no feedback (packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/text-format-group.tsx:174-178, button at :310-325), opted in by slides at packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/text-edit-section.tsx:89-94 and toolbar/mobile-toolbar.tsx:576-580, routed through packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts:650-652 to the same caret-only implementation. It is the only unlink path in slides: `onLinkRequest` is unwired (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/slides-view.tsx:738-749) and CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE omits `href` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:300-315, rationale at text-editor.ts:3422-3424). `expandRangeForLinks` (link-run.ts:207-233) only snaps partial drags and does not cover a wider selection, so it is not a guard against this path. Real, reachable, user-visible silent failure of the advertised operation at a site outside the diff's guard — major.

finding.summary: The toolbar/EditorAPI Clear-formatting path still extends a hyperlink at its trailing edge — the fix this delta added to `TextEditor.clearFormatting` was not propagated to `EditorAPI.clearInlineFormatting`
finding.evidence: `EditorAPI.clearInlineFormatting` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3344-3350) routes into `applyStyleImpl`, whose collapsed-caret branch is `pending.set({ ...getSelectionStyleImpl(), ...style }, cursor.position)` (editor.ts:1167-1174). `getSelectionStyleImpl` → `caretInlineStyle` returns the run the caret sits in, and at a link's trailing edge (`position.offset <= inlineEnd`) that run's style INCLUDES `href` (packages/docs/src/model/caret-style.ts:71-78). Since this PR removed `href` from `CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE`, the constant no longer overrides it, so the staged pending style keeps `href: 'https://…'`. Nothing re-arms the exit for an ordinary typed character — `exitLinkIfAtTrailingEdge` is only called on space (text-editor.ts:980-982), Enter (2608, 2641) and paste (4171) — so click Clear formatting with a collapsed caret at the end of a link, type `x`, and the `x` is inside the link. This is exactly the regression the delta guards against on the keyboard path (text-editor.ts:3440-3448) and the case the new test `Cmd+\ at a link trailing edge still exits the link` covers; the toolbar entry point has no equivalent guard or test. The docs design doc claims parity for all three entry points (docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md:263-284), which is now inaccurate for the toolbar. Fix belongs in `applyStyleImpl`'s collapsed branch (or in `clearInlineFormatting` before delegating), mirroring the trailing-edge re-arm.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `EditorAPI.clearInlineFormatting` bare-delegates to `applyStyleImpl(CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE)` with no trailing-edge override, so the toolbar path still extends a hyperlink. The actual body (editor.ts:3344-3373) computes `const exitsLink = collapsed && (isAtLinkTrailingEdge(doc, cursor.position) || !!(prev && 'href' in prev && prev.href === undefined))` and calls `applyStyleImpl(exitsLink ? { ...CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE, href: undefined } : CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE)` — i.e. it uses the same shared `isAtLinkTrailingEdge` helper the keyboard path uses (imported at editor.ts:29; used at text-editor.ts:3441 and text-editor.ts:5913), and additionally preserves an already-armed exit via `pending.get()`. The helper's own doc comment (caret-style.ts:65-68) states it is shared precisely because both Clear-formatting entry points need it. The claim of "no equivalent test" is also false: link-trailing-edge.test.ts:266-278 exercises `editor.clearInlineFormatting()` then typing `x` and asserts the trailing run's href is falsy, with over-reach guards at :280-292 (caret inside link) and :294-308 (range selection). The described defective code is not present at the cited location.

finding.summary: Cmd+\ now wipes the trailing-edge `href: undefined` pending style, so typing after a clear at a link's end extends the hyperlink
finding.evidence: exitLinkIfAtTrailingEdge (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:5918-5922) arms pending with { ...visual, href: undefined } so the next typed character escapes the link. clearFormatting() (:3431) *replaces* that pending state with CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE, which no longer contains an href key at all; createPendingStyle.set (packages/docs/src/view/pending-style.ts:22) overwrites rather than merges, and an absent key in the merge patch means "leave the run's value alone", so text typed after Cmd+\ at a link's trailing edge now inherits the neighbouring run's href. Previously the shortcut's own list carried href: undefined and preserved the escape. The docs toolbar path has the same shape at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1170, where the caret style (including the live href) is merged under the clear patch.

verdict.reason: The claimed code is not present. `TextEditor.clearFormatting()` does not replace the pending style with a bare `CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE`: at packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:3439-3448 it computes `exitsLink = isAtLinkTrailingEdge(this.doc, this.cursor.position) || (prev && 'href' in prev && prev.href === undefined)` and sets `{ ...CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE, href: undefined }` when true — the second disjunct exists specifically to preserve the `href: undefined` that `exitLinkIfAtTrailingEdge` (text-editor.ts:5912-5917) armed, so the trailing-edge escape survives Cmd+\. The docs toolbar path has the same explicit override: `clearInlineFormatting` at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3362-3372 computes the same `collapsed && (isAtLinkTrailingEdge(...) || prev.href === undefined)` condition and passes `{ ...CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE, href: undefined }` into `applyStyleImpl`, so the caret-style merge at editor.ts:1170 cannot re-arm the link. The guard is non-vacuous: `isAtLinkTrailingEdge` (packages/docs/src/model/caret-style.ts:70-87) really tests caret-at-run-end with an `href` whose next run does not continue it. `pending.set` does replace rather than merge (packages/docs/src/view/pending-style.ts:22-24), which is exactly why both call sites carry the explicit `href: undefined` re-arm.
